# Data and study design

## Redd data and reaches

```{r a1-numbers}
n_redds <- nrow(redds)
n_reach <- n_distinct(redds$COMID)
n_ry <- n_distinct(redds$key)
yrs_reach <- redds |>
  distinct(COMID, year) |>
  count(COMID)
n_multi <- sum(yrs_reach$n >= 2)
n_all4 <- sum(yrs_reach$n == 4)
lens <- rev_tab("F4_comid_random_intercepts.csv")
```

Chinook salmon redds were surveyed every 3--5 days from the onset of redd construction in late July to the end of spawning in mid-September, 2002--2005, in eight streams of the Middle Fork Salmon River. Spawn date was taken as the first date a completed redd was observed and expressed as day of year on a non-leap calendar (dates in 2004 after 28 February shifted back one day), so that the same calendar date has the same value in every year. Data from 2001 and from Knapp and Cape Horn creeks were excluded because they were not sampled consistently. The analysis dataset contains `r format(n_redds, big.mark = ",")` redds in `r n_reach` reaches and `r n_ry` reach-years (@tbl-a1-survey).

Each redd location was joined to the NHDPlus Version 2 flowline network, and each flowline segment (identified by its COMID) is treated as a *reach*. Reaches are the units for which Siegel et al. (2023) predict daily stream temperature. Surveyed reaches are short: median `r sprintf("%.2f", median(lens$length_km))` km (range `r sprintf("%.2f", min(lens$length_km))`--`r sprintf("%.2f", max(lens$length_km))` km). Every reach belongs to one stream, so reaches are nested within streams. `r n_multi` reaches were surveyed in two or more years and `r n_all4` in all four years; these multi-year reaches contain `r format(sum(redds$COMID %in% yrs_reach$COMID[yrs_reach$n >= 2]), big.mark = ",")` of the redds and carry the within-reach (between-year) temperature contrast used in the final model (Section A4).

```{r}
#| label: tbl-a1-survey
#| tbl-cap: "Redds by stream and year, number of reaches, and elevation range of surveyed reaches."
surv <- redds |>
  count(stream, year) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = year, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
  left_join(
    redds |> group_by(stream) |> summarise(Redds = n(), Reaches = n_distinct(COMID)),
    by = "stream"
  ) |>
  left_join(
    rev_tab(
      "F5_elevation_span_by_stream.csv"
    ) |>
      transmute(stream, `Elevation (m)` = sprintf("%.0f–%.0f", elev_min, elev_max)),
    by = "stream"
  ) |>
  rename(Stream = stream)
surv <- bind_rows(
  surv |>
    mutate(across(where(is.numeric), as.character)), tibble(
    Stream = "Total",
    `2002` = as.character(sum(redds$year == 2002)), `2003` = as.character(sum(redds$year == 2003)),
    `2004` = as.character(sum(redds$year == 2004)), `2005` = as.character(sum(redds$year == 2005)),
    Redds = as.character(n_redds), Reaches = as.character(n_reach), `Elevation (m)` = ""
  )
)
kbl2(surv, align = "lrrrrrrr")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-a1-structure
#| fig-cap: "Sampling structure. (A) Number of reaches per stream. (B) Number of redds per reach. (C) Number of years each reach was surveyed."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 2.8
pa <- redds |>
  distinct(stream, COMID) |>
  count(stream) |>
  ggplot(aes(n, fct_rev(stream), fill = stream)) +
  geom_col() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = cols.streams, guide = "none") +
  labs(x = "Reaches", y = NULL)
pb <- redds |>
  count(COMID) |>
  ggplot(aes(n)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 5, fill = "grey60", color = "black") +
  labs(x = "Redds per reach", y = "Reaches")
pc <- yrs_reach |> ggplot(aes(factor(n))) +
  geom_bar(fill = "grey60", color = "black") +
  labs(x = "Years surveyed", y = "Reaches")
pa + pb + pc + plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-a1-reach-dates
#| fig-cap: "Spawn dates by reach within each stream. Boxes show the interquartile range; points are individual redds. Reaches are ordered by drainage area (upstream at top)."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 8.5
da <- lens |>
  select(COMID, da_km2) |>
  mutate(COMID = as.character(COMID))
redds |>
  left_join(da, by = "COMID") |>
  mutate(COMID = fct_reorder(COMID, -da_km2)) |>
  ggplot(aes(fixed_date + yday, COMID)) +
  facet_wrap(~stream, scales = "free_y", ncol = 2) +
  geom_boxplot(aes(fill = stream), outlier.shape = NA, linewidth = 0.25) +
  geom_jitter(height = 0.15, size = 0.3, alpha = 0.3) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = cols.streams, guide = "none") +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "2 weeks", date_labels = "%d %b") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank())
```

## Stream temperature

Daily stream temperatures were taken from the reach-scale model of Siegel et al. (2023), which agreed closely with logger data in Idaho (@fig-a1-siegel). @fig-a1-thermal shows the modeled thermal regime of each stream in each year, the window used for the thermal index (Section A3), and the observed spawning period.

```{r}
#| label: fig-a1-thermal
#| fig-cap: !expr 'paste0("Modeled mean daily stream temperature across surveyed reaches, by stream and year (Siegel et al. 2023). Grey band: window of the thermal index (", INDEX_N, "-d mean, ", doy_lab(INDEX_END_DOY - INDEX_N + 1), "–", doy_lab(INDEX_END_DOY), "). Blue band: range of observed spawn dates.")'
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 7.5
temps |>
  left_join(redds |> distinct(COMID, stream), by = "COMID") |>
  filter(doy >= 91, doy <= 305) |>
  group_by(stream, year, doy) |>
  summarise(temp = mean(temp, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(fixed_date + doy, temp, color = factor(year))) +
  annotate("rect",
    xmin = fixed_date + INDEX_END_DOY - INDEX_N + 1, xmax = fixed_date + INDEX_END_DOY,
    ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, fill = "grey85"
  ) +
  annotate("rect",
    xmin = fixed_date + min(redds$yday), xmax = fixed_date + max(redds$yday),
    ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.15
  ) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.5) +
  facet_wrap(~stream, ncol = 2) +
  scale_color_manual(values = cols.years) +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "1 month", date_labels = "%b") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Mean daily stream temperature (°C)", color = "Year") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-a1-siegel
#| fig-cap: "Comparison of modeled daily stream temperatures (Siegel et al. 2023) with empirical logger observations (Isaak et al.)."
#| out-width: "75%"
# Rasterised copy of plots/Figure_isaak-siegel-compare.pdf (an 11.7 MB vector
```
